photo.caption: The leverage ratio, measured as debt divided by equity, for investment bank Goldman Sachs from 2003–2012. The lower the ratio, the greater the ability of the firm to withstand losses.
photo.description: Bar chart showing the leverage ratio for Goldman-Sachs from 2003-2012. The leverage ratio (debt divided by equity) is a measure of the risk taken. The higher the ratio, the more risk undertaken.
